It's not about the port, necessarily, it's about what's going in and out of that port. You can change the used port in your torrent program. The default torrent ports in many torrent programs (6881-6889) are monitored, blocked, or throttled by many ISPs. (Looking at you, Comcast.) I always go for something way up in the list - 46573 or 51835 or something, since most of the Chinese and Pooinloo bots that roam the internet won't bother scanning that high.

Of course, all this assumes that you have opened your selected port in your firewall.

I will say that torrenting is the main reason I use a VPN, and PIA performs well enough for me that I've been using them for over three years now, and while it's not as fast as my bareback connection, it's fast enough for my tastes.

The one, and only one time it crashed, it was while I had torrents running, and the connections defaulted to my actual IP.

This, again, is something you need to handle on your end. In QBitTorrent, for example, you go into the settings and configure the client to run on the network device that PIA created when it was installed. That way, when the connection is dropped or lost or resets for any reason, torrents stop running (since it's configured network adaptor is unavailable) until you restart the program. PIA even has a built-in "kill switch" that shuts down all network activity if and when the VPN connection is lost. Why would you not use that if you're using your connection for less-than-scrupulous activities?

AFAIK, PIA shitcanned their user forums like six months or a year ago, but you can always put in a support ticket and get help. They're friendly enough. Some documentation still exists or has been archived if you take the time to search for it.
